note: The OLG adequately covers child support income when declared (positive allegation). The 'Child Support Income - SNAP' page instructs workers to always ask about child support when children are in the household. DOR child support is verified via MobiusView/RAPID (verified upon receipt, checked at every application/IR/recert). Non-DOR child support is verified via a letter from the payer stating amount, frequency, and intent. BEACON entry procedures are thorough. However, the OLG does not address the FNS two-step negative allegation process: when a household denies receiving child support, FNS requires (1) checking the child support enforcement agency and whether the absent parent is incarcerated, and (2) if not resolved, exploring direct/voluntary payments, attempting contact with the potentially liable person, and verifying through the child support agency. The OLG also lacks guidance on family violence sensitivity specific to SNAP child support income verification — the extensive DV pages (Domestic Violence Specialists, Good Cause) are TAFDC-focused for child support cooperation requirements and explicitly note 'DV Waivers and Child Support cooperation rules do not apply to EAEDC and SNAP-only cases.' There is no OLG guidance on resolving conflicts between a client's statement and an absent parent's statement about support payments, or on documenting decisions not to contact an absent parent due to safety concerns in the SNAP income verification context.
